newsitem.title: INDONESIA: JAKARTA CALL MONEY HIGH ON TIGHT LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: JAKARTA CALL MONEY HIGH ON TIGHT LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Jakarta call money remained expensive on Thursday on the back of sustained tight money market liquidity, dealers said.
Overnight money eased to 30.0 percent from 50 percent. Longer-term rates were driven higher, with one-week money at 29.0 percent, one-month at 23.0 and six at 20.0 percent.
A balance of 223 billion rupiah was available to the market from the maturing central bank papers.
Dealers said interest rates were inversed, suggesting the temporary nature of the condition.
"What people need is short-term money. Many bought dollars earlier, so they need the rupiah now," one dealer said, adding that it was not surprising that the market was extremely tight.
Central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said the bank had intervened with some $500 million on Wednesday to support the rupiah after speculative attacks.
"We have anticipated the tightening," the dealer said. "The bank had squeezed the short-end market. The intervention will drain additional rupiah from the market."
He said the absence of short-term securities (SBPUs) facilities added to market woes.

Dealers said the central bank was trying to contain market speculative dollar buying with its interest rate policy and announcement that it would stop publishing formal intervention limits for the rupiah.
The central bank maintained its bilateral rates for central bank certificates (SBIs) after raising them by 100 basis points on Wednesday.

The bank kept its overnight SBIs at 15.0 percent, four-to-six day SBIs at 16.0 percent, one-week at 10.5, two-week at 11.0, one-month at 11.625, three at 11.5, six at 12.125 and one-year at 12.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 23.69 percent, compared with 18.97 percent on Tuesday.
